articles.title: How to Build an MVP App: Core Features vs Full Build
articles.excerpt: When figuring out how to build an MVP app, the most important step is defining the smallest version of your product that you can launch to solve a real user problem. Founders and developers often face…
articles.body: When figuring out how to build an MVP app, the most important step is defining the smallest version of your product that you can launch to solve a real user problem. Founders and developers often face the temptation to pack every possible feature into the initial release. Building an application triggers the urge to pile on user management, complex dashboards, and multi-layered permissions before writing a production line of code. The lean startup methodology counters this by forcing a strict definition of actual utility. Understanding the minimum viable product approach An MVP focuses strictly on the core problem your users face daily while cutting out secondary features like dark mode or deep analytics for version one.

articles.title: When you replace a library, you also take over everything it did
articles.excerpt: DPOLens is an open-source MCP server that gives AI assistants the text of privacy law. Its search runs on the CPU, so it needs no GPU. The usual way to run an embedding model in Python is sentence-tra…
articles.body: DPOLens is an open-source MCP server that gives AI assistants the text of privacy law. Its search runs on the CPU, so it needs no GPU. The usual way to run an embedding model in Python is sentence-transformers . DPOLens doesn't use it: with PyTorch's CPU build it installs about 1 GB, against about 200 MB for ONNX Runtime , the tokenizers library and NumPy. So DPOLens calls the model through ONNX Runtime directly, and does the tokenising and pooling itself, in about forty lines. Those forty lines did their job. What they didn't do was what the library does without being asked. When a new instance starts for the first time, it embeds every clause of the law it carries , and while load-testing the community version , I found that this was the heaviest thing DPOLens ever did.

articles.title: Bitwarden vs 1Password vs Proton Pass: Which Is Best?
articles.excerpt: Your password manager is the most important security tool you use daily. Pick the wrong one, and you're either compromising security (weak encryption) or compromising convenience (so annoying to use t…
articles.body: Your password manager is the most important security tool you use daily. Pick the wrong one, and you're either compromising security (weak encryption) or compromising convenience (so annoying to use that you start cutting corners). After 60 days with each of the top three — Bitwarden, 1Password, and Proton Pass — here's the real breakdown. The Short Version Bitwarden: Best for individuals and teams who want open-source, auditable security at the lowest price. Self-hosting available. 1Password: Best for families and non-technical users who want the most polished, user-friendly experience. Security model is excellent but not open-source. Proton Pass: Best for privacy maximalists already in the Proton ecosystem. Good but not great as a standalone password manager.

articles.body: Wondering whether Telegram is safe from hackers comes down to understanding how the app handles your messages. As of 20 November 2026, standard cloud chats on Telegram are not end-to-end encrypted by default, leaving your conversations open to server-side access if security measures are not configured properly. Many users assume that popular messaging apps protect all data equally, but architectural choices dictate how messages travel from one device to another. What happened to default security on Telegram The biggest misconception surrounding Telegram is that it is end-to-end encrypted by default for all chats. According to the Telegram FAQ , standard cloud chats are not end-to-end encrypted by default.

articles.title: Designing a Practice Mode That Cannot Touch Your Streak
articles.excerpt: Here is a design bug that looks like a feature: a practice mode that occasionally counts as a real run. Players notice. They stop trusting the streak, and a streak you do not trust is a streak nobody…
articles.body: Here is a design bug that looks like a feature: a practice mode that occasionally counts as a real run. Players notice. They stop trusting the streak, and a streak you do not trust is a streak nobody keeps. The fix is not to hide practice mode. It is to make the two states provably separate, and then to say so out loud. Separate the counters, then separate the rewards A streak counter that can be incremented by two different code paths will eventually be incremented by both. If the practice screen and the daily screen share a write function, the boundary is a convention rather than a guarantee. The robust shape is two counters, two write functions, and a single place where the daily counter is incremented — from the daily completion handler and nowhere else.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998:  Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. It was just one piece, but the foundation of something much larger.
articles.body: On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station.

articles.body: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.
